verdict.rationale: GrowthBook's own documented design supports leaving: it can be self-hosted on your own infrastructure and MongoDB, experiment data stays in your own warehouse, a full REST API exposes the data (including experiment results 'into your own reporting'), and OpenFeature means switching away needs only a provider change. However, no documented 'export all data' feature or open-format bulk export exists in the evidence, so exiting means assembling API calls or database access yourself. Missing for 10: a documented one-step full-data export, the export file formats, and hands-on or independent confirmation of a complete migration out.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can export all of my data in open formats and leave

citations.quote: Switching from or to GrowthBook only requires changing the provider bootstrap, not a single flag call.
GrowthBook offers a full REST API for interacting with the application.
Run GrowthBook on your own infrastructure with Docker Compose, including MongoDB, the API, and the front-end.
Warehouse Native. Query 11 data sources including BigQuery, Snowflake, and Databricks.
Get results for an experiment (`GET /v1/experiments/{id}/results`) to pull the latest analysis into your own reporting.
